CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Bungo Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Government is the Government of Bungo Regency.
4. Regent hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Bungo.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in the administration of governmental affairs that are the authority of the region.
6. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPAA is a regional technical implementation unit established by the Regional Government in providing services for women who experience violence, discrimination, special protection, and other problems.
7. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, handling and empowerment.
8. Discrimination is any differentiation, harassment or exclusion that is direct or indirect based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, tribe, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and basic freedoms in life both individual and collective in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields and other aspects of life.
9. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without using means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life and body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
10. Violence against women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic and social exploitation, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
11. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
12. Prevention is an effort made by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women from occurring.
13. Family are persons who have a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and collateral lines up to the third degree, or who have a marital relationship, or persons who are dependents of a woman.
14. Community is individuals, families, communities, religious leaders, community leaders, traditional leaders, business world and corporations, community organizations, social organizations, women and gender study centers, mass media or other similar entities.
15. Private sector is Non-Governmental Institutions, the Business World and Mass Media.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes acts that result in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, loss of pregnancy (miscarriage), fainting and/or cause the death of women.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering in women.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c includes:
 a. acts in the form of sexual harassment;
 b. forced sexual intercourse;
 c. forced unnatural sexual intercourse, and/or
 d. forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter d includes:
 a. acts of economic or sexual exploitation with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; and/or
 b. acts, with or without the consent of the victim, which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, exploitation of the physical body, sexual aspects, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or exploiting the labor or ability of a person by other parties to obtain benefits both material and immaterial.

Article 3
The Objectives of Protection of Women by Regional Government include:
a. Preventing all forms of violence against women
b. Providing protection and services to women victims of gender-based violence; and
c. Providing services for the recovery of the physical, psychological and economic conditions of women victims of violence.

Article 11
(1) Protection of Women provided by the Regional Government includes:
a. prevention;
b. services;
c. empowerment; and
d. coordination of Protection of Women.
(2) Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner by the Regional Government through the Regional Apparatus administering governmental affairs that fall under the Region’s authority in the field of women’s empowerment.
(3) The Regional Apparatus administering governmental affairs that fall under the Region’s authority in the field of women’s empowerment, in providing Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1), shall establish UPTD PPA.
(4) Further provisions regarding UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (3) shall be regulated by a Regent’s Regulation.

Second Part
Rights of Women Victims of Violence

Article 26
(1) Regional Government based on cooperation as referred to in Article 25 establishes partnerships in providing Protection for Women.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. provision of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence,
b. education and training for women victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women victims of violence; and
d. fostering and increasing economic independence for women victims of violence.

6.2.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, the regulation defines “Perdagangan Orang” (trafficking in persons) in Pasal 1 angka 11, but the operative provisions on rights/services are framed generally for “perempuan korban kekerasan” (women victims of violence) and forms of violence in Pasal 6–7 (fisik/psikis/seksual/eksploitasi/penelantaran). Nowhere does the regulation explicitly recognize or provide specific protection/services for “perempuan korban perdagangan orang” (women victims of trafficking) as a distinct intersectional group. A mere definition (and even citing the national anti-trafficking law in the ‘Mengingat’ section) does not establish that the policy addresses women victims of trafficking under the protection framework. The retrieved English candidates correctly reflected this: they only showed the definition of trafficking and general victim protections, not trafficking-specific provisions. The judge incorrectly inferred coverage from the presence of a definition, leading to a false positive; thus this is an evaluation/logic error rather than a translation or retrieval failure.
